# Product foundation

## Product
Chaser sends polite payment reminders and collects payment for freelance designers, so they stop chasing late invoices by hand.

## Problem
Late invoices hurt, and designers hate asking for money. Today they keep a spreadsheet and write awkward emails weeks after the due date, or let it slide. This costs a few hours a month.

## Persona
A freelance brand or web designer who works alone, with 3 to 10 active clients. They invoice from a tool like Wave or from a PDF. They want to get paid on time without asking for money themselves. What stops them: they hate the ask, so they put it off or skip it.

## Not for
1. Agencies with a finance person.
2. Freelancers outside design (developers, writers, consultants). We turn them away at sign-up.

Open: whether to turn away designers with more than 10 clients.

## Goals
1. 50 paying users by the end of March 2027. A paying user is any user on a paid plan, at any price.
2. $5,000 monthly revenue by the end of December 2027.

## Anti-goals
1. We will not build invoicing itself. Open: why (not stated).
2. No mobile app. Open: why (not stated).

## Assumptions
1. Designers will let a tool email their clients in their name. Not yet proven.
2. Designers will let Chaser collect payment from their clients. Not yet proven.

Open: price. Goals count paying users and revenue, but no price or plan exists.
Open: how reminders reach clients beyond email, if at all.
Open: how Chaser learns of an invoice (import from Wave, PDF upload, or manual entry).

questions.question: Should sign-up turn away freelancers outside design, or only leave them out of our marketing?
questions.why: Sign-up cannot check who is a designer, and turning away developers or writers who would pay works against the goal of 50 paying users.

questions.question: Which designers count: brand and web only, or also graphic, UI/UX, illustrators and motion designers?
questions.why: The product line says freelance designers but the Persona says brand or web, so two readers picture different people and Not for has no line for the rest.

questions.question: Do designers with more than 10 clients belong in Persona or in Not for?
questions.why: They have the most late invoices and the most to gain, so turning them away may lose the best payers, and the open line leaves the 3 to 10 range as either a target or a limit.

questions.question: Would you ever have Chaser create or send invoices, and if not, why?
questions.why: Invoicing is the most tempting add-on for this product, and the reason decides whether it is a never or a not-yet.

questions.question: Will Chaser ever escalate past polite reminders, such as late fees, firm notices, or handing debts to collectors?
questions.why: Escalation is the obvious next step when polite reminders fail, and it conflicts with the promise that designers never have to ask harshly.

questions.question: Why no mobile app, and does a phone-friendly web page count as one?
questions.why: Without a reason, the team cannot tell whether responsive web, push alerts, or a client-facing pay page are allowed.

questions.question: What monthly price do you expect a typical paying designer to pay?
questions.why: 50 users reach $5,000 a month only at $100 each, so price decides whether Goal 2 needs far more users than Goal 1 sets.

questions.question: Does Goal 2's revenue mean only subscription fees, or also a cut of collected payments?
questions.why: A fee on collected invoices could reach $5,000 with few users, which changes the target and the user count Goal 1 needs.

questions.question: Should Goal 1's paying user have a minimum monthly price?
questions.why: As written, 50 users on a $1 plan meets Goal 1 while missing Goal 2 by a wide margin.
